**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ 

- The precious complex was driven lower in a risk averse week where Italian bonds traded above 7 % and the IMF mentioned concerns over the Chinese financial sector. Gold dropped on Friday to below the opening price on November the 1st, giving up the monthly gains, and as we have seen, the price has dropped sharply since Friday’s action. What is probably still confusing to observers is the manner in which the European crisis—and the inability of euro zone politicians to devise a policy response, having devised any number of ways to deny that it was a crisis— has failed to ignite gold. 

• The futures positioning in gold indicates that recent buyers may be struggling with poor averages owing to the recent drop in value. Palladium  has seen a particularly sharp price drop given the recent length added to the market and we will be keen to see developments in the next round of CFTC figures. 

- In the ETF sector, gold saw continued buying as investors still seek the insurance quality of gold, but the remaining metals see either liquidation or a investors sidelining themselves.

Many longs and other interested observers must be wondering what kind of market developments are good for the gold price, as we see the installation of technocrats (not necessarily a bad thing in the short term) instead of democratically elected governments., and no sign of a decision. Realistically, the ECB cannot break the law and buy up Italian debt—but the market is making the judgement that it might be able to finesse some panEuropean version of QE that is more about flooding the market with liquidity and not simply backstopping fiscally unsound governments. Gold should have some support at the Ichimoku cloud base at $1673-1674. - In the gold market, investor interest rose for the fourth successive week with net long speculative positions on COMEX climbing by three quarters of a million Troy Ounces to almost 27 million ounces. Fresh buying was noted in almost equal size from both large and small specs in Comex futures, and given that almost 2 million troy ounces of buying has been seen since the 1st of November, and prices are today back to or close to levels at the beginning of the month, the implication is that there are recent longs who will struggle with a poor average price. - Gold ETF holdings climbed again, by almost a million ounces, with the SPDR being the most conspicuous home for ETF money. As with the futures, buyers bought into price weakness, but will be under less pressure to sell. - Silver had something of a rout last week as we dipped towards the mid-October lows on risk aversion. Using Italian 10 –year government securities as a mark of risk-aversion, yields ran up from a weekly low of 6.33 pct on Monday to a high of 7.144 on Thursday, with silver making corresponding drops in price to hit a low of $30.92 basis Decembers last Friday. The overall trend for silver is still ‘down’, with a short term target of $29.25. A break of $35.50 looks necessary to get - Net long speculative interest in silver on COMEX increased by 5.64million ounces to 165 million ounces in the week to the 15th of November. Open interest dropped by over 6.60 million ounces, indicating that there has been a reduction in shorts on last weeks savage drop in prices. Overall, since the 4 Oct CFTC figures, a rising trend of large spec longs from the low of 59.50 million ounces to current levels is becoming apparent, despite more or less trendless price action. - Silver ETF positioning fell by almost 2 million ounces last week to 460 million ounces. - The platinum price dropped almost $80 from the highs after Europe continued to be deadlocked on the policy decisions necessary to solve debt concerns. Technically speaking, Platinum was only just able to close at the 50 % retracement of the big Sept-Oct drop before turning lower. The medium term trend remains ‘negative’ and the concerns of wealth destruction in the Euro combined with concerns over Chinese ‘vulnerabilities’ (pace the first IMF evaluation of the Chinese financial sector.) The interim review of platinum given by Johnson Matthey mid-week expected growth of 2.2 pct in 2011, to 8.08 million tozs, predicated on increasing demand from the Diesel sector, and an increase in net demand of 10 pct in the Chinese jewellery sector. Asian flat panel glass investment also appears to remain robust. - Japanese investors returned as buyers, with light buying also noted in COMEX to total around 1 MT of investor buying. Some short-covering took place during the week as shorts took profits on the dip. - Platinum ETF holdings increased slightly by 6,000 Tozs with buying noted from the US ETF Securities. - Palladium could not really break above the previous weeks highs in the $675 area and with the growing anxiety over Italy and even the thought of contagion spreading to France, where a 55 bp move in debt maturing in 2021 represents a decent deterioration in the course of 1 week. (As mentioned earlier, 10 year Italian debt worsened by 80 bp at one point in the week.) The recent rally from the $535 low looks to have broken down, and a re-test of $565-570 levels is likely, basis our daily point and figure. The move through $630 last week looks to have triggered some dealer stops. The intermediate term trend is ‘negative’. During the week, JM gave an interim forecast of Palladium’s price of between $500-800, relatively bearish compared to the forecast 6 months previously, reflecting weak economic conditions. - Net long positions in palladium continue to rise, adding almost 40,000 ounces. Between Tuesday the 25th Oct and the 15th of November, around 127,000 Tozs of investor net buying was added on the futures. The December futures price closed at $652.10 on the 25th of October so with the price dropping through $630 since last Tuesday, it will be interesting to observe any chances in positioning in next weeks CFTC report, basis the figures for the 22nd of November.. - Palladium ETF remained unchanged over the course of the week. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** ### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
